title: Accelerator Fleet Reconciler: Terraform module for mixed ASG/Karpenter GPU pools in Private VPC
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a reusable Terraform module (accelerator-fleet-reconciler) that provisions and reconciles GPU/accelerator node pools across two autoscaling modes (ASG for reserved/legacy pools and Karpenter for ephemeral/spot-friendly pools) inside Redwood Private/VPC deployments. The module must include upgrade-safe workflows, automated driver/kernel compatibility checks, health probes, graceful draining hooks, spot fallback rules, and observability hooks for console dashboards. It should integrate with existing private VPC networking, KMS-backed secrets for node bootstrap, and our migration tooling for rolling kernel/driver updates.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module can create both ASG-backed and Karpenter-backed accelerator pools from the same root module with minimal flags
Module exposes inputs for instance families, accelerator types, ami/launch template overrides, spot percentages, and max_unavailable for upgrades
Health checks: node-level readiness/liveness probes plus control-plane reconciliation metrics emitted (prometheus labels) and visible in console runtime-graphs
Upgrade path: safe in-place driver/AMI upgrades with canary pool, cordon/drain hooks, and automatic rollback on node-failure threshold
Fallback: when spot capacity exhausted, ASG fallback/overflow group created automatically (configurable) and workload placement policy documented
E2E test: Terraform plan/apply pipeline for a staging Private cluster runs and validates node lifecycle and metric emissions
technical_decisions: Expose two submodules (asg_pool, karpenter_pool) behind a single root module so infra teams can use a single module reference
Use a reconciliation controller pattern in Terraform: module produces state tags and a small Kubernetes operator (helm chart) will reconcile node annotations for upgrade orchestration
Implement driver/AMI validation as an external data source that runs a small instance in a test subnet to validate nvml and kernel modules before tagging an AMI as 'validated'
Prefer instance change over rolling node replacement when driver ABI remains compatible; otherwise trigger full cordon/drain and replace with validated AMI
Emit metrics via CloudWatch -> Prometheus bridge (existing pipeline) using standardized metric names: redwood.accel.reconciler.*
plan_steps: Draft Terraform API and input/output contract (inputs: accel_types, instance_profiles, spot_ratio, fallback_asg_config, health_probe_config)
Prototype module locally against a staging Private cluster (use existing test VPC)
Build small validation runner (Go binary) packaged as user-data to test AMI driver compatibility
Integrate helm chart for the reconciliation helper into module outputs and add values that point to created resources
Write acceptance tests (terratest) to simulate AMI upgrades, spot exhaustion, and forced node failures
Coordinate with Console team to add dashboard tiles and alerting rules for new metrics
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Terraform-based reconciliation could be slow for fast autoscaling churn. Mitigation: keep reconciler responsibilities lightweight; rely on Karpenter/ASG for short-term scaling decisions and use reconciler only for long-lived invariants and upgrades.

Risk: Driver/AMI validation failures could block upgrades for many clusters. Mitigation: allow manual override and staged canary channel; add automated rollback windows and verbose failure reasons in logs.
Risk: Increased blast radius when fallback ASG launches many on-demand instances. Mitigation: add budget caps and rate limits; require approval for >X on-demand instances per cluster.
Risk: Security exposure from node bootstrap secrets. Mitigation: require KMS encryption for all bootstrap secrets, rotate test-runner credentials, and add audit-log hooks in module outputs.
testing_and_qa: Unit tests for Terraform module using terraform-compliance and kitchen-terraform
Terratest E2E pipeline: create a small Private cluster, provision module, run simulated spot interruption, validate fallback and draining
Chaos run: terminate nodes mid-upgrade and assert rollback triggers and service continuity
Manual review: infra eng + runtime + console signoff on dashboards and alerts
rollout_plan: Deploy module to internal staging namespaces first (staging VPC) and run canary AMI upgrades
Open beta: enable module for 2 small customer private clusters with monitoring and additional runbook support
Gradual rollout over 3 weeks with weekly checkpoints; halt on alert spike or increased 5xx error rate
GA: publish documentation in internal Confluence and example usages in terraform-redwood-modules repo
rollback_plan: If canary nodes fail beyond threshold: trigger terraform apply with previous validated_ami input and set max_unavailable to 100% to quickly converge
If fallback ASG causes cost or capacity issues: disable fallback flag and scale down via API, notify on-call
If reconciliation helm chart misbehaves: revert chart values via helm rollback and remove reconciler annotation from cluster
